books.title: The Tenant of Wildfell Hall
books.author: Anne Brontë
books.desc: A mysterious young widow and her son move into a ruined old house, stirring village gossip, until her diary reveals the marriage she has escaped.
about: A young woman calling herself Mrs Helen Graham settles with her small son at Wildfell Hall, a half-ruined old house in a quiet country parish. Her reserve and independence set the neighbours talking, while the young farmer Gilbert Markham, who tells the story in letters to a friend, is drawn to her despite the rumours. To answer his doubts, Helen gives him her diary, which tells the story of her past.

Anne Brontë writes with unusual frankness about alcoholism, cruelty and the near-total power a husband held over his wife and child under the law of the time. The novel defends a woman's right to protect herself and her son, and combines a realistic picture of a dissolute circle of gentlemen with Helen's firm moral courage.

The Tenant of Wildfell Hall was published by Thomas Cautley Newby in June 1848 under the pen name Acton Bell. It was very popular and controversial, and many reviewers attacked it as coarse and shocking. It was Anne Brontë's second and last novel, and is now often described as one of the first feminist novels.

books.title: Villette
books.author: Charlotte Brontë
books.desc: Alone and without fortune, Lucy Snowe crosses to a foreign city to teach at a girls' school, where she hides a passionate heart behind a calm face.
about: After a series of family misfortunes leaves her alone in the world, the quiet and observant Lucy Snowe travels from England to Villette, the capital of a small European kingdom, and finds work in a girls' boarding school run by the watchful Madame Beck. There, among strangers who speak another language and follow another faith, she meets the handsome English doctor John Graham Bretton and the fiery, irritable teacher Monsieur Paul Emanuel.

Narrated by Lucy herself, guarded and often unreliable about her own feelings, the novel is an intense study of loneliness, self-reliance, longing and faith. Brontë draws on her own time in Brussels, which Villette is modelled on, and blends sharp observation, Gothic touches and psychological depth.

Villette was published in three volumes by Smith, Elder and Co. on 27 January 1853, under the pen name Currer Bell. It was the third and last novel Charlotte Brontë published in her lifetime, and many critics consider it her finest work.

books.title: The Pickwick Papers
books.author: Charles Dickens
books.desc: Kind-hearted Mr Pickwick and his friends set off to explore England, and with his sharp-witted servant Sam Weller tumble from one comic adventure into the next.
about: Mr Samuel Pickwick, the generous and innocent founder of the Pickwick Club, sets out with three friends, the romantic Tupman, the poetic Snodgrass and the would-be sportsman Winkle, to travel England and report on what they see. Coaching inns, elections, cricket matches, Christmas festivities and the schemes of the swindler Alfred Jingle fill their journeys, and Mr Pickwick soon gains a devoted servant in the cheerful Londoner Sam Weller.

Dickens's first novel is a loose series of comic episodes that grows into a warm story about friendship, good nature and the follies of the world. Its humour, lively dialogue and gallery of eccentrics, with Sam Weller and his father Tony at the centre, made it one of the most popular comic books ever written.

Published in monthly parts from April 1836 to November 1837 by Chapman and Hall, under the full title The Posthumous Papers of the Pickwick Club, it was written when Dickens was only twenty-four. The original illustrator, Robert Seymour, died after the first instalments. The book became a runaway success and made Dickens famous.

books.title: Waverley
books.author: Walter Scott
books.desc: A dreamy young English officer is drawn into the Scottish Highlands and the Jacobite rising of 1745, torn between loyalty, romance and rebellion.
about: Edward Waverley, a romantic young Englishman raised on old books, takes a commission in the army and goes to Scotland. Visiting the old Baron of Bradwardine and his gentle daughter Rose, he is drawn on into the Highlands, where he meets the clan chief Fergus Mac-Ivor and his proud, passionately Jacobite sister Flora, just as Prince Charles Edward Stuart prepares the rising of 1745.

Scott follows a hero caught between two worlds, Hanoverian England and the old clan society of the Highlands, and shows history through the lives of ordinary and extraordinary people. The novel mixes adventure, romance, humour and Scots dialogue with a sympathetic and clear-eyed view of a lost cause.

Waverley was published anonymously in 1814 and was Scott's first novel. Its great success gave its name to the long series of Waverley novels that followed, and it is often regarded as one of the first historical novels in the Western tradition.

books.title: The Castle of Otranto
books.author: Horace Walpole
books.desc: When a giant helmet falls from the sky on his wedding day, the tyrant Manfred's dark ambitions unleash secrets and wonders in the first Gothic novel.
about: Manfred, Prince of Otranto, is anxious to see his sickly son Conrad married to the young Isabella, for an old prophecy hangs over his family's hold on the castle. On the wedding day Conrad is crushed beneath a gigantic helmet that falls mysteriously into the courtyard. Desperate to secure an heir, Manfred turns his attentions to Isabella herself, who flees through the castle's underground passages, while a young peasant named Theodore becomes entangled in the strange events.

Walpole set out to combine the marvels of old romances with the natural characters of modern fiction. Haunted portraits, secret passages, prophecies, persecuted heroines and hidden identities fill this short and fast-moving tale, and many of its devices became standard features of Gothic fiction.

The Castle of Otranto was first published on 24 December 1764 under a pretence: Walpole presented it as a translation of an old Italian manuscript. In the second edition he acknowledged his authorship and added the subtitle A Gothic Story. It is generally regarded as the first Gothic novel.
books.author_short: English writer, antiquarian and politician (1717–1797), author of The Castle of Otranto and builder of Strawberry Hill.
author_long: Horatio Walpole, known as Horace, was born in London on 24 September 1717, the youngest son of the Prime Minister Sir Robert Walpole. He became a Whig member of Parliament, an art historian and an antiquarian, and late in life succeeded as 4th Earl of Orford. At Twickenham, near London, he built Strawberry Hill, a house that revived the Gothic style decades before the Victorians. He died on 2 March 1797.

Walpole is remembered above all for The Castle of Otranto (1764), generally regarded as the first Gothic novel, and for his letters. More than 3,000 of them survive, covering the years 1732 to 1797, and they give a lively and detailed picture of Georgian England.
